newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia to review decree on alcohol - report.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia to review decree on alcohol - report.

text.p: Indonesia will re-evaluate a decree that increases liquor levies and places new controls on distribution following a call by Islamic groups for a total alcohol ban, the Jakarta Post newspaper reported Thursday.
"I will issue an instruction to re-evaluate the decree on alcoholic beverages soon," Home Minister Yogie Memet was quoted as saying.
He did not give further details, the newspaper said.
Moslems were enraged earlier this month when the Jakarta municipal government passed the decree.
Islamic groups said the move would raise money for the government from undesirable sources and sanction alcohol consumption in what is mainly a Moslem society.
Fifteen of Indonesia's 27 provinces, including Jakarta, have already passed the decree.

Hasan Basri, leader of the powerful Islamic Council of Ulemas (MUI), called earlier this month for a ban on alcohol until any changes to distribution regulations can be made. He proposed that distribution be strictly controlled thereafter.
But Yogie ruled out a complete ban on alcohol.
"The government cannot completely prohibit alcohol. There are areas in the country where local customs dictate that people can drink alcoholic beverages," Yogie was quoted as saying.
Indonesia's population of 190 million people is 85 percent Moslem, but alcohol is freely available in most areas.
